questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What is Cardiac Sonography?
questions.explanation: Echocardiography is defined by being both non-invasive (probe on the body surface, no ionizing radiation) and real-time (live moving images of the beating heart). Because options A and B are each true, the best answer combines them. *(Practice review slide 3.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What is the most common modality used in Echocardiography?
questions.explanation: TTE is the first-line, routine echo exam: the transducer is placed on the chest wall, it requires no sedation, and it is fully non-invasive. *(Practice review slide 5.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What do Cardiac Sonographers NOT do?
options: Use independent judgment to add images/measurements based on findings
questions.explanation: Producing the final signed diagnostic report is the responsibility of the interpreting physician (cardiologist), not the sonographer — so this is the task outside the sonographer's scope. *(Practice review slide 7.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What is a characteristic of 2D imaging (TTE)?
options: Graphical representation of direction and velocity of blood flow
Visual representation of hemodynamics in real time
questions.explanation: 2D imaging produces real-time tomographic (cross-sectional) slices of the heart from multiple standardized planes and windows — the anatomic backbone of the exam. *(Practice review slide 9.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What is a characteristic of M-Mode Imaging?
options: Direction and velocity of myocardial motion vs time
questions.explanation: M-mode samples a single ultrasound line at a very high frame rate, displaying the motion of structures along that line over time — historically called the “ice-pick” view. *(Practice review slide 11.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What is a characteristic of Colour Doppler?
options: Blue shows blood flow travelling towards the transducer
Red shows blood flow travelling away from the transducer
Does not demonstrate velocity of blood flow
Red shows blood flow travelling towards the transducer
questions.explanation: Color Doppler follows the BART convention — Blue Away, Red Toward — so red encodes flow moving toward the transducer. *(Practice review slide 13.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What is a characteristic of Spectral Doppler?
options: Single perpendicular axis giving rapidly updated single-line images
Displays structure and function of cardiac anatomy
Graphical representation of direction and velocity of blood flow
questions.explanation: Spectral Doppler (PW and CW) plots blood-flow velocity against time, showing both direction (above/below baseline) and magnitude as a waveform. *(Practice review slide 15.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What is a characteristic of Tissue Doppler?
options: Most accurate for timing and measurements
Direction and velocity of myocardial motion vs time
questions.explanation: Tissue Doppler imaging (TDI) measures the low-velocity, high-amplitude motion of the myocardium itself over time — for example mitral annular e′. *(Practice review slide 17.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What are the steps to perform before scanning your patient?
options: Look at the requisition for the indication for the exam
Determine if there are any clinical symptoms
questions.explanation: All three are essential pre-scan steps — history, requisition/indication, and current symptoms together drive an appropriate, indication-tailored protocol. *(Practice review slide 19.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Which of the following is a possible indication?
questions.explanation: Both angina (chest pain of cardiac origin) and a heart murmur are recognized indications for echocardiography, so the combined answer is best. *(Practice review slide 21.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What kind of transducer is used in TTE?
questions.explanation: TTE uses a phased-array transducer: a small footprint fits between the ribs, and electronic beam steering forms the wide sector image of the heart. *(Practice review slide 23.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What does focus control on the image?
options: Where the beam converges, improving resolution
Appropriate depth to display anatomy in the field of view
Width of the field of view
Increase/decrease of the overall amplitude of echoes
questions.explanation: The focus sets the focal zone — the depth where the beam is narrowest — which optimizes lateral resolution at the region of interest. *(Practice review slide 25.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  How many apical imaging planes are there?
questions.explanation: There are four standard apical planes: apical 4-chamber, 2-chamber, 3-chamber (apical long-axis) and 5-chamber. *(Practice review slide 27.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What does Time Gain Compensation control on the image?
options: Increase/decrease of echo amplitude in a vertical segment
Increase/decrease of echo amplitude in a horizontal segment
Increase/decrease in echo amplitude in the far field only
Increase/decrease of the overall amplitude of echoes
questions.explanation: TGC adjusts echo amplitude at a specific depth — a horizontal band of the image — to compensate for attenuation as sound travels deeper. *(Practice review slide 29.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What does Lateral Gain Compensation control on the image?
options: Increase/decrease in echo amplitude in the far field only
Increase/decrease of echo amplitude in a vertical segment
Increase/decrease of echo amplitude in a horizontal segment
Increase/decrease of the overall amplitude of echoes
questions.explanation: Lateral Gain Compensation adjusts echo amplitude across the side-to-side (lateral) dimension — vertical segments/columns of the sector. *(Practice review slide 31.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What position is the patient in for the Parasternal window?
questions.explanation: Left lateral decubitus rolls the heart toward the chest wall and displaces lung, opening the parasternal acoustic window. *(Practice review slide 33.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What position is the patient in for the apical window?
questions.explanation: The apical window also uses left lateral decubitus — often a steeper roll — to bring the true apex against the chest wall (or bed cut-out). *(Practice review slide 35.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What position is the patient in for the subcostal window?
questions.explanation: Supine with the knees bent relaxes the abdominal wall, letting the transducer angle up under the costal margin toward the heart. *(Practice review slide 37.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What position is the patient in for the suprasternal window?
questions.explanation: Supine with the neck extended (often a pillow under the shoulders) exposes the suprasternal notch for imaging the aortic arch. *(Practice review slide 39.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What characteristic does the PEDOF probe have?
options: Most commonly used in adult echo
Small probe with a long arm
questions.explanation: The PEDOF (Pedoff) probe is a dedicated continuous-wave 'pencil' Doppler transducer — it produces only a spectral Doppler trace, with no 2D image. *(Practice review slide 41.)*

questions.explanation: There are four standard apical planes: apical 4-chamber, 2-chamber, 3-chamber (apical long-axis) and 5-chamber. *(Practice review slide 27.)*

questions.stem: During a mock adult echocardiography board examination, consider the following.  What does Time Gain Compensation control on the image?
options: Increase/decrease of echo amplitude in a horizontal segment
Increase/decrease of echo amplitude in a vertical segment
Increase/decrease in echo amplitude in the far field only
Increase/decrease of the overall amplitude of echoes
questions.explanation: TGC adjusts echo amplitude at a specific depth — a horizontal band of the image — to compensate for attenuation as sound travels deeper. *(Practice review slide 29.)*

questions.stem: During a mock adult echocardiography board examination, consider the following.  What does Lateral Gain Compensation control on the image?
options: Increase/decrease of echo amplitude in a horizontal segment
Increase/decrease of echo amplitude in a vertical segment
Increase/decrease in echo amplitude in the far field only
Increase/decrease of the overall amplitude of echoes
questions.explanation: Lateral Gain Compensation adjusts echo amplitude across the side-to-side (lateral) dimension — vertical segments/columns of the sector. *(Practice review slide 31.)*

questions.stem: During a mock adult echocardiography board examination, consider the following.  What position is the patient in for the Parasternal window?
questions.explanation: Left lateral decubitus rolls the heart toward the chest wall and displaces lung, opening the parasternal acoustic window. *(Practice review slide 33.)*

questions.stem: During a mock adult echocardiography board examination, consider the following.  What position is the patient in for the apical window?
questions.explanation: The apical window also uses left lateral decubitus — often a steeper roll — to bring the true apex against the chest wall (or bed cut-out). *(Practice review slide 35.)*

questions.stem: During a mock adult echocardiography board examination, consider the following.  What position is the patient in for the subcostal window?
questions.explanation: Supine with the knees bent relaxes the abdominal wall, letting the transducer angle up under the costal margin toward the heart. *(Practice review slide 37.)*

questions.stem: During a mock adult echocardiography board examination, consider the following.  What position is the patient in for the suprasternal window?
questions.explanation: Supine with the neck extended (often a pillow under the shoulders) exposes the suprasternal notch for imaging the aortic arch. *(Practice review slide 39.)*

questions.stem: During a mock adult echocardiography board examination, consider the following.  What characteristic does the PEDOF probe have?
options: Small probe with a long arm
Most commonly used in adult echo
questions.explanation: The PEDOF (Pedoff) probe is a dedicated continuous-wave 'pencil' Doppler transducer — it produces only a spectral Doppler trace, with no 2D image. *(Practice review slide 41.)*

questions.stem: A sonographer is reviewing the relevant anatomy, technique, or physiology.  What is Cardiac Sonography?
questions.explanation: Echocardiography is defined by being both non-invasive (probe on the body surface, no ionizing radiation) and real-time (live moving images of the beating heart). Because options A and B are each true, the best answer combines them. *(Practice review slide 3.)*

questions.stem: A sonographer is reviewing the relevant anatomy, technique, or physiology.  What is the most common modality used in Echocardiography?
questions.explanation: TTE is the first-line, routine echo exam: the transducer is placed on the chest wall, it requires no sedation, and it is fully non-invasive. *(Practice review slide 5.)*

questions.stem: A sonographer is reviewing the relevant anatomy, technique, or physiology.  What do Cardiac Sonographers NOT do?
options: Use independent judgment to add images/measurements based on findings
questions.explanation: Producing the final signed diagnostic report is the responsibility of the interpreting physician (cardiologist), not the sonographer — so this is the task outside the sonographer's scope. *(Practice review slide 7.)*

questions.stem: A sonographer is reviewing the relevant anatomy, technique, or physiology.  What is a characteristic of 2D imaging (TTE)?
options: Graphical representation of direction and velocity of blood flow
Visual representation of hemodynamics in real time
questions.explanation: 2D imaging produces real-time tomographic (cross-sectional) slices of the heart from multiple standardized planes and windows — the anatomic backbone of the exam. *(Practice review slide 9.)*

questions.stem: A sonographer is reviewing the relevant anatomy, technique, or physiology.  What is a characteristic of M-Mode Imaging?
options: Direction and velocity of myocardial motion vs time
questions.explanation: M-mode samples a single ultrasound line at a very high frame rate, displaying the motion of structures along that line over time — historically called the “ice-pick” view. *(Practice review slide 11.)*

questions.stem: A sonographer is reviewing the relevant anatomy, technique, or physiology.  What is a characteristic of Colour Doppler?
options: Red shows blood flow travelling away from the transducer
Red shows blood flow travelling towards the transducer
Does not demonstrate velocity of blood flow
Blue shows blood flow travelling towards the transducer
questions.explanation: Color Doppler follows the BART convention — Blue Away, Red Toward — so red encodes flow moving toward the transducer. *(Practice review slide 13.)*

questions.stem: A sonographer is reviewing the relevant anatomy, technique, or physiology.  What is a characteristic of Spectral Doppler?
options: Graphical representation of direction and velocity of blood flow
Displays structure and function of cardiac anatomy
Single perpendicular axis giving rapidly updated single-line images
questions.explanation: Spectral Doppler (PW and CW) plots blood-flow velocity against time, showing both direction (above/below baseline) and magnitude as a waveform. *(Practice review slide 15.)*

questions.stem: A sonographer is reviewing the relevant anatomy, technique, or physiology.  What is a characteristic of Tissue Doppler?
options: Direction and velocity of myocardial motion vs time
Most accurate for timing and measurements
questions.explanation: Tissue Doppler imaging (TDI) measures the low-velocity, high-amplitude motion of the myocardium itself over time — for example mitral annular e′. *(Practice review slide 17.)*

questions.stem: A sonographer is reviewing the relevant anatomy, technique, or physiology.  What are the steps to perform before scanning your patient?
options: Look at the requisition for the indication for the exam
Determine if there are any clinical symptoms
questions.explanation: All three are essential pre-scan steps — history, requisition/indication, and current symptoms together drive an appropriate, indication-tailored protocol. *(Practice review slide 19.)*

questions.stem: A sonographer is reviewing the relevant anatomy, technique, or physiology.  Which of the following is a possible indication?
questions.explanation: Both angina (chest pain of cardiac origin) and a heart murmur are recognized indications for echocardiography, so the combined answer is best. *(Practice review slide 21.)*

questions.stem: A sonographer is reviewing the relevant anatomy, technique, or physiology.  What kind of transducer is used in TTE?
questions.explanation: TTE uses a phased-array transducer: a small footprint fits between the ribs, and electronic beam steering forms the wide sector image of the heart. *(Practice review slide 23.)*

questions.stem: A sonographer is reviewing the relevant anatomy, technique, or physiology.  What does focus control on the image?
options: Width of the field of view
Increase/decrease of the overall amplitude of echoes
Where the beam converges, improving resolution
Appropriate depth to display anatomy in the field of view
questions.explanation: The focus sets the focal zone — the depth where the beam is narrowest — which optimizes lateral resolution at the region of interest. *(Practice review slide 25.)*
